_comment: The agent harness configuration. ONE file, two readers (config.ps1 for the
scripts, config.py for the Mattermost bridge), so a value is never defined
twice in two languages. Precedence, resolved only in the loaders:
built-in defaults < this file < harness.local.json (gitignored) < environment
This file is committed and MUST NOT contain secrets - it holds policy and
topology only. Machine-specific or experimental overrides go in

extension._why_locked: operator 2026-08-28: the surface the operator drives interactively must never silently degrade to a weaker model.

mattermost._note: switchable in a thread with 'profile: <name>', the same shape as the existing 'model:' and 'worktree:' directives.

claude-code._note: a Claude Code agent - a subagent in an editor session, or 'claude -p' spawned by the bridge. Model names are CLI aliases, not API ids.

little-coder._note: the local substrate: little-coder reaches llama-cpp through LiteLLM. Wired and callable, but no work item has completed through it yet - do not read config support as a proven feature.

fixture._note: scaffolding for the quadrant comparison's own proof: performs an item deterministically with no model at all. status 'self-test' is load-bearing - quadrant/schema.json's comparable_runner_statuses excludes it, so it can never appear in a decision table, and test_quadrant.py asserts no profile assigns a role to it.

_comment: The TARGET axis (PLAN 1 L3), orthogonal to the runner axis and living in
configuration rather than code: 'Nothing in the pipeline layer knows which

self._note: the org works on ai-stack itself: a worktree off the operator's loaded branch, plane leases for shared runtime, this repo's branch policy. The quadrant harness uses a DETACHED worktree so a comparison never leaves a branch behind.

project._note: the org pointed at an external project: agent-org's clone/workspace model, git-proxy containment, the GitHub App as the door. For a COMPARISON the workspace is a local disposable repo - a comparison must never be the first thing to touch a real target.

_comment: The runner x target comparison (PLAN 2, U4: 'same anchored item run per
quadrant (runner x target), outcomes compared'). Listing the axes here
rather than in code is what lets a fifth runner or a third target be a
config edit; the harness derives the matrix, and its report always renders
one row per configured cell whether or not that cell produced a record.
quadrant._repeats_note: 1 means every cell is n=1 and the report says so in those words. Raise it to 2+ before treating any difference between quadrants as real.
quadrant._results_dir_note: NOT under .claude/. Measured 2026-08-30: a claude-code run whose workspace lived at .claude/quadrant-runs/.../workspace had every Write and Edit turned into a permission request - Claude Code treats .claude/ as a sensitive path - so the quadrant scored 1/2 on a task the model had already solved correctly in its reply. The harness would have been measuring its own directory choice.

all-cloud._desc: the default everywhere; all three roles on cloud opus

all-local._desc: no cloud calls at all; needs the inference plane healthy

local-work-cloud-review._desc: cheap production, expensive judgement - the reviewer is the last gate before a merge

cloud-work-local-test._desc: expensive production, cheap verification - useful when the test plan is mechanical

pipeline._note: the role -> state -> duty table stays in queue.ps1: it is behavior, not tuning. Turning a gate off here is an operator decision with a real cost, which is why both are listed explicitly rather than assumed.

_env_files_note: Runtime files a worktree needs but git will not materialize. The two recipe
.env files live INSIDE the OB1 submodule, so a fresh worktree clone never has
them and `docker compose -f OB1/docker/docker-compose.yml config` fails there
while passing in the main checkout - which is how the offline harness came to
fail only in worktrees. An ARRAY of lines, like _comment above: a JSON string
cannot contain a raw newline, and the first version of this note did. PowerShell
ConvertFrom-Json accepted it; Python json.loads did not - and this file has BOTH
readers (config.ps1 and config.py), so it would have broken the bridge alone.
